test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
With reference to medieval history, consider the following statements.

1. The founder of the Chola dynasty called the 'Imperial Cholas' was Vijayalaya (9th century AD).

2. One of the important dynasties which ruled in northern India was Gurjara-Pratiharas.

3. Palas ruled in western India and Rashtrakutas ruled in southern India in the early years (750 -1000).

Which of the given statement(s) is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vijayalaya Chola** was the founder of the Imperial Chola dynasty in the 9th century AD, marking the resurgence of the Chola power in South India.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratiharas were one of the most significant dynasties ruling northern India during the medieval period, recognized for their contributions to art, architecture, and defense against Arab invasions.
 
• The Palas ruled eastern India (Bengal and Bihar), not western India, during the early medieval period (750–1000 AD).
 
• The Rashtrakutas were a prominent dynasty that ruled southern and parts of central India during the same era, known for their patronage of art, literature, and architecture.
 
• Statements 1 and 2 are correct, while statement 3 inaccurately places the Palas in western India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Imperial Cholas:** The Chola dynasty reached its zenith under rulers like Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, known for their naval dominance and architectural marvels like the Brihadeshwara Temple.
 
• **Gurjara-Pratiharas:** They were instrumental in defending India from Arab invasions and contributed significantly to the development of temple architecture, including the Khajuraho temples.
 
• **Palas Dynasty:** Originating in Bengal, they are renowned for their patronage of Buddhism, leading to the establishment of institutions like Nalanda and Vikramashila.
 
• **Rashtrakutas:** Known for the Ellora caves, particularly the Kailasa temple, Rashtrakutas were patrons of art and culture while maintaining expansive trade networks.
 
• **Medieval India Chronology:** The period from 750–1000 AD saw the emergence of several regional powers, each contributing uniquely to the political, cultural, and economic fabric of India.
